Annotators judged each generated sentence for fluency (binary grammatical correctness) and compared pairs of generated and reference arguments for persuasiveness.

Two aspects are evaluated: fluency and persuasiveness. We consider a sentence as fluent if it is grammatically correct, i.e. contains neither semantic nor syntactic errors, and arrange this as a binary task. To reduce subjectivity for the persuasiveness evaluation, the experts do not annotate single arguments but instead compare pairs of generated and reference data arguments.
